Subject: Post-call recap: data handling & retention (next steps)

Hi Sarah — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of ask:
- FinCo needs to ensure PII from user prompts is not retained beyond the session (0-retention for PII).
- Limited operational logs for debugging are acceptable but should be shortened (proposed 30 days).
- Data residency: US only for production workload.

Recap of what we covered:
- Redwood can support per-customer retention policies (hosted + Dedicated/private options).
- Two options we discussed: 1) Hosted with Enhanced Privacy add-on + retention exception (short logs), or 2) Private deployment for strict retention controls (longer timeline).

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm the exact PII scope (examples of fields you consider PII).
2) We'll loop in Security to confirm what we can commit in writing for a pilot (0-retention for transcripts + 30-day truncated logs for non-PII telemetry).
3) I'll send the Data Retention Exception form and our SOC2 report for your security review; Marissa (CC) will confirm the exact language for the SOW redline.
4) If acceptable, we’ll prepare a DocuSign SOW with the retention exception and pricing impact for the pilot.

Attachments: — I’ll attach the exception form and SOC2 in the next email.

Thanks,
Camila

Camila — thanks for the summary. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we loop legal:

- "0-retention for PII": can you confirm whether that means we will have no persisted transcript or request logs that contain PII fields? Will any transient caches be written to disk?
- For analytics/usage metrics we need aggregated non-identifying metrics retained for at least 90 days. Is that compatible with the 30-day operational logs you mentioned?
- Can you send the Data Retention Exception form you referenced, and SOC2 report? Our security team will want to see specifics on logging (token logs, request headers, metadata).

Also, what's the expected timeline for getting an exception in writing? We have a pilot window starting July 6th and need to confirm controls before kickoff.

Thanks Sarah — answering inline below and attaching the exception form so your security/legal can start reviewing.

> "0-retention for PII": can you confirm whether that means we will have no persisted transcript or request logs that contain PII fields? Will any transient caches be written to disk?

- Short answer: we can commit to no persisted request transcripts that contain customer-designated PII fields for the pilot (we treat "PII fields" as names, SSNs, payment card numbers, and other identifiers you specify). Our runtime can be configured to strip configured fields server-side before logging. KV/prefix caches are ephemeral and can be configured to be in-memory only; for hosted deployments we’ll ensure they are not persisted to long-term storage for the scope of the pilot. (Marissa, please confirm formal language.)

> For analytics/usage metrics we need aggregated non-identifying metrics retained for at least 90 days. Is that compatible with the 30-day operational logs you mentioned?

- Yes — we differentiate operational token-level logs (for debugging) from aggregated analytics. We can retain aggregated non-identifying metrics for 90 days while limiting token-level logs to 30 days.

> Can you send the Data Retention Exception form you referenced, and SOC2 report?

- Attached: data-retention-exception-form.pdf (fillable), and we will attach our SOC2 report in the next message from Marissa.

Timeline:
- If security sign-off is quick, we can deliver the signed exception and updated SOW within 5 business days. For your July 6 pilot start, that should be achievable if we get feedback this week.

Next steps: please have security/legal review the attached form and list the PII fields you want excluded. I’ll coordinate with Marissa to finalize the SOW redline and pricing impact.

Attachment: data-retention-exception-form.pdf

Best,
Camila
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-16T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: data handling & retention (next steps)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the questions. Looping in a quick, security-oriented answer and the SOC2 report for your review (attached). Below are the concrete commitments we can make for the pilot and the SOW language we propose.

Pilot commitments (FinCo-specific):
- PII definition & scope: Redwood will rely on the customer-provided list of PII fields (the attached exception form has a section for this). For the pilot, we’ll treat values matching those fields as PII.
- 0-retention for PII: Redwood will not persist request/response transcripts that contain the designated PII fields beyond the session boundary. Any request data containing PII will be stripped server-side prior to being written to persistent logs.
- Ephemeral caches: KV/prefix caches used to support context are kept in memory and not persisted for the pilot. We will disable checkpointing for this customer for the pilot window.
- Operational logs: token-level request logs used for debugging will be retained for 30 days and then purged. Aggregated, de-identified metrics (latency, token consumption, error rates) will be retained up to 90 days per your need.
- Data residency: production traffic will be routed to US-only regions for this account.

SOW & legal notes:
- We can include the above as an appendix to the SOW. We will provide a redline (redline_sow.docx) showing the exception clause. Please note: a formal legal exception requires sign-off from Redwood legal if the exception extends beyond the pilot or modifies default retention SLAs.
- Operational impact & pricing: there is no change for the hosted pilot if we can implement the field-stripping rule and 30-day logs. If FinCo later requires a guarantee of zero-persistence at the filesystem level (e.g., Dedicated/private or FIPS/HSM-backed keys), that typically maps to the Enhanced Privacy add-on or Private deployment which has a pricing delta. I can share a ballpark if we get a sense of expected volume.

Attachments: soc2-report-2025.pdf, redline_sow.docx

Please confirm the PII list in the exception form and we’ll issue the updated SOW. If you want, we can also provision a short-term Dedicated node for the pilot to provide stronger controls (longer lead time).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
